chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who fasted, then thought that the sun had set while there were clouds in the sky, so he broke his fast. Then the clouds cleared, and suddenly the sun had not set. He said: “His fast has been completed, and he does not make it up.”

key_terms.ٱلشَّمْسَ: the sun, as the sign for sunset ending the fast

ai.seo_question: If someone breaks the fast thinking the sun has set, then discovers it had not set, must the fast be made up?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a fasting person who breaks the fast due to a mistaken assumption that sunset has occurred because of cloud cover. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that the fast remains valid and no make-up fast is required in this case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1901 - Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:

"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who was fasting and thought the sun had set because the sky was cloudy, so he broke his fast. Then the clouds cleared, and it became evident that the sun had not yet set.
Imam (as) said: 'His fast is complete, and he does not need to make it up.'"
